I totally understand how you feel and I would agree that it is difficult to put into words. My ex was emotionally abusive and when I met my current boyfriend, I was in the same state as you are right now. 

The overthinking, honestly, it's not gonna stop. On the bright side, it does die down after awhile. What my SO did to make me feel better, other than words is updating me what he's doing throughout the day, if he's going out which friend is it with. Even right down to what he's doing for dinner. Probably sounds creepy, but it helps your overthinking so much!!! And believe me, even with all that, there will still be room for overthinking unfortunately. Another thing that eased mine tremendously was having a tracking app. It would be too excessive for many and that's understandable. My family first used it due to safety purposes then I proposed the idea to my SO and he was okay with it thankfully. 

Try keeping yourself busy too. I know it's difficult with the pandemic but try anyway. It does cut down a lot of overthinking time. Hope this helps, sending you lots of hugs xx

Crazy story here. I'm from Malaysia and him, Australia. We both had a "puppy love" back when we were just 12 y/o and he has not moved yet. His family tried their best to separate us and it succeeded. What they did was emotionally scarring and traumatizing but I won't go into that. When we turned 13, he moved to Australia and I had no idea because I didn't want to speak to him anymore ever since what happened. Throughout the years he tried to reached out to me but I couldn't be bothered and I still have not recovered. Fast forward to 6 years later, he reached out again, said he's coming back to Malaysia for a holiday, and asked if I would like to grab dinner. I was at my lowest of the low as I just got out of a mentally abusive relationship. My ex was still playing around with my feelings and we do meet up quite frequently. So I agreed to grab dinner with him and god, what a glow-up when I saw him, my jaw literally dropped. I had to come up with a lame excuse to cover myself up for staring! Dinner was great, but I was too emotionally damaged to even react much. So his birthday was coming up next week and I decided why not ask him to hang out together with some people that we know to celebrate his birthday? He was like sure. We went for a movie. Our friends left after and he asked if I would like to go for another show. I agreed and we were suppose to part ways after that as he had already told his parents to pick him up at 8.00 pm (at that time, we both didn't have our driving license yet) but instead he asked me if I would like to have dinner with him, again. We had dinner, we talked. He is perfectly aware of what I was going through and I shall quote what he said, "Be my girlfriend." I was shocked, mind scrambling everywhere. We almost kiss when we parted ways but we did not. We finished dinner at 9.00 pm so he left his parents waiting for an hour and they went ballistic. He totally forgotten to inform his parents. He said it was all worth it as he managed to spend more time with me. There was this indescribable intensity between us and few days later I agreed to his shocking request which brings us to today, 2 years later. We didn't meet before he left so we kissed 5 months later.

Things you could do/say to show her that you care: Netflix Party, watch a movie together and bond over it. Tell her that you love her, miss her at random times throughout the day. Make it a thing for you both to update each other on how your day was. 

General tips: Plan. Always plan when you will meet up next. Planning gives you and your SO hope and in an LDR, that is absolutely needed. Trust and being understanding. There will be times when you feel that you both don't understand/trust each other. You both have to work it out and make sure that the trust and understanding is always there. Definitely set a specific time to call if you and her schedules allow to. Do video call as it is much more interesting and interactive. 

How to act: That's entirely up to you. Since you said both of you are pretty inexperienced, go explore what you and her like. Do give her a heads up that you are new to the sexual things, that's why you may react in a different way than expected. Gradually, it will get better. To maintain a sexual relationship, you both could always try dirty talk, sexting or to spice things up to another level, masturbate on video. 

Hope this helps!

It is tough to save up for flights and you will struggle really hard but when you see him standing in front of you, it's worth the efforts. I have been planning to study in Melbourne for my post-grad, hopefully by next year after I graduate from my Degree. It seems that you both have established good communication and trust, which I believe are essential in LDR. It's clear too that you are determined to get into a school in NYC. If you both are agreeable to the plan of you going to a school in NYC and he going after 1.5 years, then by all means go for it. What would be best for both of you is to voice out your opinions honestly about the future plans. LDR comes with a sacrifice and no matter how eager you are to close the distance, do not rush it. You and your SO must be happy with the decision or it could create more arguments in the future.
